messages:
Anya: Proposal — add a token-cost guard to rollout evaluator. If avg tokens per req or derived cost spikes we should auto-pause canary. Thoughts?

Mike: +1 in principle. We need to agree on window, aggregation (mean vs p95), and what action (pause vs throttle). Also fail-open vs fail-closed?

Liam: Prefer fail-closed for latency/errors. For cost I'm more tolerant but noisy signals matter. Suggest 5m sliding window, p95 for latency, avg for tokens, min_samples=200. :thinking: 

Sara: UX note — console must show which guard fired, severity, and provide quick actions: pause, reduce traffic, rollback, open incident. Also allow manual override for first responders.

Anya: Draft config so we can iterate:
```yaml
rollout:
  name: canary-2026-03
  traffic_split: 10
  guards:
    - name: token_cost
      metric: tokens_per_request
      window_seconds: 300
      operator: ">"
      threshold: 1500
      severity: critical
      action: pause
      min_samples: 100
    - name: latency_p95
      metric: latency_p95_ms
      window_seconds: 300
      operator: ">"
      threshold: 1200
      severity: critical
      action: rollback
    - name: error_rate
      metric: error_rate
      window_seconds: 300
      operator: ">"
      threshold: 0.02
      severity: warn
      action: reduce_traffic
      reduce_to_percent: 5
```

Mike: How do we translate tokens -> dollars? We need a per-model unit_cost that can change (quantization, model swap). Should we evaluate both tokens*unit_cost and billing_cost where available and prioritize billing_cost.

Liam: Telemetry caveat — ensure token counts come from post-deduped telemetry (no double counting cached prefixes). Also include sample-size checks to avoid flapping on very low traffic.

Anya: Edge case: model quantization changes cost without token change. Proposal: guard accepts multiple metrics and fallback logic:
```pseudo
metric = billing_cost if billing_cost.available else tokens_per_request * model_unit_cost
```
This lets us act even when billing pipeline lags.

Sara: Console wire — highlight metric timeline, sample size, affected routes, and button "pause + open incident". Add a tooltip: "reduces false positives by requiring min_samples".

Mike: Also add hysteresis/backoff: don't unpause immediately; require stable below-threshold for 10m and gradually ramp traffic.

Liam: Agree. Also test harness request: we need a simulator to inject token spikes and verify guard behavior, plus alerts when guard misfires.

deploy-bot: Rollout policy updated in staging: canary-2026-03 (guards added) — see /deploys/1234

Anya: Action items: Mike to add unit_cost lookup, Liam to add min_samples and hysteresis in evaluator, Sara to wire up UI states. We'll reconvene after staging run. Thanks.
